title: Affine source case of flat counit presentations
statement: Let p:Y -> B and g:A -> B be scheme morphisms with B and A affine, and let U be an affine open of Y. For every quasi-coherent O_U-module N flat over U -> Y -> B, there is a StandardSingleFlatCounitPresentation for this composite morphism, N and g. No flatness of g, global compactness of Y, or relative separatedness of p is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A1D, affine calculation for M[0]; Tag 0DJ9, initial affine case; original model proof Step 1

proof.text: Put f = U.ι followed by p. Both its source and target are affine, so f is affine. For every pair W contained in V of affine opens of B, f inverse image W is affine. Apply relative flatness to V and that inverse image. The direct-image section module is definitionally N(f inverse image W); naturality of f.app identifies its scalar action with restriction along the identity appLE on B. Hence f_*N is flat over the identity of B. Apply affine-local intrinsic flatness implies tensor flatness.

Take the concrete complex K = (f_*N)[0]. Let D be the homotopy single complex of N. The single/direct-image isomorphism rho identifies quotient K with the termwise direct image of D. Prove affine pushforward acyclicity by dimension shifting: injective modules are flasque and Cech-acyclic; quasi-coherent modules are Cech-acyclic on affine opens; this class is stable under cokernels of monomorphisms; on affine inverse images Cech exactness makes pushforward preserve the epimorphism in a short exact sequence. Apply Functor.rightAcyclic_of_epi_map_g, then isIso_canonicalSingleDirectImageMap and cancel the single-complex comparison to make the right-derived unit beta at D invertible. These are the already proved lower Cech tools, used directly to avoid the cyclic import through DirectImage.AffineMorphism and FiniteFreeComplex. Set e to the inverse of Qh(rho) followed by beta. Tensor pullback of N is quasi-coherent, and the base-changed morphism f prime is affine, so the target right-derived unit is invertible as well. Ordinary affine base change makes termwise exchange on D invertible: its degree-zero component is the affine exchange of N, and in every other degree its source and target are zero. Define t as Qh of pulled-back rho, Qh of exchange, the target derived unit, and Rf prime of the single/pullback identification, in that order.

Expand picardTermwiseSingleMap on N. Functoriality and the hom-inverse equation for the left-adjoint comparison cancel that comparison, leaving the pinned counit followed by Qh of the single/pullback identification. Apply derivedBaseChange_unit_compatibility to D. Precompose with Lg of Qh(rho) and postcompose with Rf prime of the single/pullback identification. Naturality of the pinned g-counit moves rho past it. These composites are exactly Lg(e inverse) followed by standardSingleBaseChangeMap and the pinned counit followed by t. Cancel Lg(e inverse), which is an isomorphism. No pullback counit is inverted.

Bound K by zero using the zero terms of the single complex. Its degree-zero term is isomorphic to f_*N and is flat by the first step; all other terms are zero and tensor-flat. Combine this bound and flatness with the explicit e, t and their equation. This constructs the required presentation for every N, including zero modules and empty affine source opens.

    (g : A ⟶ B) (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    StandardSingleFlatCounitOnOpen p g U
